rule: closing snapshot == opening snapshot + exactly the deltas registered here. An observed delta that is not registered is drift. A registered delta that is not observed is also drift. One more or one fewer either way fails.

why_this_register_exists.problem: OA-001 authorised one additive NSG rule. That left two bad outcomes available. If the snapshot field table omitted NSG rules, the closing check would pass while a real configuration change went unrecorded, which is a hole in the paper record. If the field table included them, the closing check would necessarily report drift and manufacture a false hard blocker at the last step of P-0.
why_this_register_exists.resolution: NSG rules were added to the snapshot field table, and the single authorised change is registered here and bound to the commit that authorised it. The change is therefore both visible and expected, and any other change remains drift.

widening_record.what_happened: The execution host's NAT egress moved outside the originally registered prefix and SSH stopped connecting at the transport layer. Addresses were observed in two discontiguous /24s within the same corporate range; the pre-existing operator rule at priority 1000 sits in the higher of the two, which confirms both belong to that range.
widening_record.action: the existing rule was widened in place to the narrowest single prefix covering every observed address
widening_record.why_not_a_second_rule: a second rule would have required a second registered delta and would have grown the register every time the pool moved; widening in place keeps exactly one registered delta and leaves the closing check unchanged in shape
widening_record.why_the_register_was_updated: a register that describes a rule which no longer exists is worse than no register; the closing check compares against what is registered, so the registration must track the authorised change

expected_deltas.spend_impact: none; a network security group rule carries no charge
expected_deltas.vm_impact: none; no VM was started, stopped, resized or reconfigured

not_registered_and_therefore_drift_if_ob: any VM size or configuration change
any modification or removal of the pre-existing NSG rule at priority 1000
any change to the cpuserver NSG
any storage account or container creation, deletion or property change
any second NSG rule beyond the one registered above
